ops.body:
- **G? [M] Where you are, now: a fresh fix when Explore or Navigate comes to the front, location off said** (2026-11-27) · Earn · aligned if reshaped
  From: /investigate, the owner's ask (2026-11-27). Brief: docs/research/current-position.md.
  Calls: one fresh fix whenever a screen that uses your position opens or comes to the front and when the app returns, nothing watching between ("Fresh fix when needed (Recommended)"); the outing and planner pages mended at once ("Fix it now (Recommended)"); location off said in the quiet notice each time Explore comes to the front, no dot or "You're here" without a fix ("Quiet notice each time (Recommended)"); a fix up to 30 minutes old used and said ("Up to 30 min, said (Recommended)"). Decision 0273, amending 0070 (NV16), keeping 0036 and NV17.
  Before it: the outing and planner pages: built in fix outing-current-position (each reads one fresh fix as it opens, says it needs your location when refused, routes Start from that fix, Q4 on both pages).
  Mock-up: not needed (mockup.md): the existing quiet notice and its words, a dot removed, one line of words.
  Done when: on the web build at 390 x 844, launched at Fox Point and the GPS moved to Cranston while the page is in the back, brought to the front: Explore leads with Cranston, "You're here", and Plan an outing proposes around Cranston; with location refused, Explore says location is off and how to turn it on, and draws no dot.
  Area: explore, navigation, tabs.
  Touches: VISION.md Never "All-day tracking" (0036: no watch between reads; tracking by default was the owner's first idea and is out), Always "Restraint" (the notice quiet); AGENTS.md "No simulation" (a position the app did not read is never drawn as you); decisions 0070 (amended by 0273), 0036, 0005, 0154 and 0172 (the notice's words), DW5 (`FRESH_FIX_MS`); specs NV16, NV17, AT1, OJ10.
  The slice: 1. Explore reads one fresh fix (`lib/locate`) each time it comes to the front, by its tab's focus or the app's return to the front, and lists, frames and says "You're here" from it; no longer once per launch (NV16 amended). 2. Navigate's ready map reads one fix when the app returns to the front, as it does on its focus (NV17). 3. Between reads nothing watches: each read ends its own watch on a fix or its timeout, and a test holds that no watch outlives a read on either screen (0036). 4. With location refused or off, each time Explore comes to the front it says the quiet notice in `LOCATION_OFF`'s words, with Open Settings on a phone; a timeout stays quiet (O21). 5. With no fix read, no walker dot is drawn on Explore and nothing says "You're here"; the areas stay where it last listed them (AT1), never drawn as you. 6. When a fresh fix does not come in time, a screen that lists or plans from where you are uses one up to 30 minutes old (`FRESH_FIX_MS`) and says so in one line (as "From where you were 20 minutes ago."); an older one is no position. 7. The e2e moves the GPS with the page in the back and brings it to the front (the Done when), and refuses location for the notice and the missing dot.
  Precedent: Apple Maps marks your position on a tap and, with Location Services off, shows an alert with the way to turn it on (verified, support.apple.com); Google Maps greys the dot and shows "the last location you visited" when it cannot find you (verified, support.google.com); Apple's HIG asks at the moment a task needs location, not at launch (verified). docs/research/adjacent-apps.md, "Know where you are when a screen lists or plans from it".
  Payoff: every outing after a drive or a day out; Explore, Navigate and the planning pages start from where you stand, and location off is never silent. Cost: M by criteria, about four source files: `app/(tabs)/explore.tsx`, `components/walk/useReady.tsx`, a small shell hook for the app's return (`AppState`, served on the web from `visibilitychange`), `locate/notice.ts`; native unverified (the read on the app's return, Open Settings from Explore's notice).
  Instead: criteria 4 and 5 alone (location off said, no dot without a fix), keeping one fix per launch.
